Status and Roadmap

Source: vignettes/articles/roadmap.Rmd
roadmap.Rmd

What is settled for RMediation, what is on hold, and what could come next. This page states only decisions already made; the last section lists candidates, not commitments. For the ecosystem view, see the mediationverse roadmap and the package status dashboard.

Where each release lives

  • CRAN serves 1.6.1.
  • GitHub carries the later releases (published as pre-releases); the development version is 1.9.0. Install with pak::pak("Data-Wise/rmediation"); the README lists the tagged install commands.
  • The News page lists every change by version.

CRAN submission is on hold

No CRAN submission is planned until a medfit release that provides fixed_x and observed mean structure is on CRAN. medfit is GitHub-only for now. When that happens, the Suggests entry for medfit rises to medfit >= 0.8.0. A later CRAN candidate must also remove or finish the SEMFit route described below, so its version will be later than the current development version.

The SEMFit route for mbco()

mbco(h0, h1, type = "asymp") accepts two fitted medfit SEMFit objects. It calls stats::anova(h1, h0), never refits, requires medfit 0.8.0 or later (older versions get a clear error), and does not need OpenMx. The OpenMx paths are unchanged. The route is no longer labeled experimental, because medfit dropped that label in 0.11.0.

Settled behavior worth knowing

  • pprodnormal3() integrates with Gauss-Legendre by default; the earlier adaptive default returned wrong values on ill-conditioned covariance (see the Technical Notes).
  • mbco_product_null() tests a*b = 0 exactly, one single-path null per branch.
  • ci(type = "asymp") labels its interval by the confidence level, and the densities are correct for very small standard errors (both in 1.9.0; see News).

Candidates for what comes next

These are open items, not promises and not dated.

  • A CRAN submission, once the criteria above are met.
  • Issue #88: releasing the defenses for OpenMx#433, tracked in the repository.
  • Keeping the documentation in step with the code; see the Cookbook and the Quick Reference.
